sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The 3D Transformation Game
sections.content: Briefly define a linear transformation as a function that maps a 3D vector space to itself while preserving grid lines and the origin. Visualize this as 'stretching' or 'rotating' a 3D wireframe box.
sections.example: Imagine a 3D character model in a game engine; when we scale or rotate the character, we are applying a linear transformation to every vertex coordinate in its mesh.

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: Basis Vectors
sections.content: Review the concept of basis vectors î (1,0,0), ĵ (0,1,0), and k̂ (0,0,1). Explain that any 3D transformation is entirely determined by where these three vectors land after the operation.
sections.example: Visualize three colored axes (Red=i, Green=j, Blue=k). Show them being moved to new positions; the final matrix is simply a 3x3 grid containing these new coordinate values.

sections.title: The Mechanism: 3x3 Matrix Multiplication
sections.content: Introduce the 3x3 matrix as the mathematical 'instruction manual'. Explain how the matrix product transforms an arbitrary vector v = (x, y, z) into v' through linear combinations of the columns.
sections.example: Demonstrate a 'Shear' transformation. Show a static cube; as the matrix columns change, the cube tilts into a slanted parallelepiped while keeping its base fixed.

sections.title: Visualizing Determinants and Volume
sections.content: Explain the concept of the determinant as a 'scaling factor' for volume. A negative determinant indicates a space inversion (reflection).
sections.example: A 1x1x1 unit cube of 'digital clay' is squashed into a flat plane (determinant = 0) or flipped inside out like a glove through a mirror.

sections.title: Synthesis & Real-world Application
sections.content: Summarize how concatenating matrices allows complex animations. Conclude by linking this to computer graphics pipelines: rotation, scaling, and projection.
sections.example: Show a robot arm: the transformation matrix calculates the arm's position in 3D space to ensure it picks up an object precisely without hitting obstacles.
